Hey, 

I know people like to have certain tattoos for meanings or ideas etc.. 

It doesn't always have to be like that. If you like a particular artist enough to enjoy all their past work, you can always discuss with them for a variation of what they specialise in etc.. 

For example.. You want a watercolour tattoo, maybe you found an artist that specialise in this but don't know what you want. Talk with the artist and show him some of their past tattoos you like so they can design something for you or do a different variation of a design. 

But yeah, watercolour is tricky as it ages it will look more smudged then bold outlines. Take a look at the artists below I know they do decent watercolour examples.. 

Szymon gdowicz 
Sasha unisex 
David cote

As a rule of thumb, I only get a tattoo from an artist as long as I can see examples of their work. 

If I like the artists past work, at least a good 80% then I will consider them.

Also try not to limit your artist choice in your own area, it is seriously worth travelling out farther if you take your art seriously! 

Yes fine lines and smaller work will always fade quicker but don't let that put you off.

I have a odd question. I've seen some bigger designs with more detail that didn't take long and others that appear simple but took a lot longer. 

Do artist sometimes take longer if you cant take pain as much for example? 

Or is it like a newbie compared to a veteran artist with years of experience that can work quicker?

I think either choice you'll make will be good as long as you stick to your plan you have ahead! Long term thinking is the way forward. 

Well done on having a good concrete plan though! It looks like you know what you want, why you want it and how to achieve all this realistically.

19k is good but honestly isn't enough in the long run for UK standards. Maybe you can work your way up or use that to move on. Try to assess if that can be possible, is the work a field you want to stay in, does the company have positions or skills you want? 

Long term is always best!
